clue.text: French biscuit? French politician consuming one with doughnut separately

indicators.note: a politician consuming things swallows them, taking them inside his name
the two swallowed items do not go in together but at two different points

blocks.note: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a, the indefinite article, means one
the letter O is ring-shaped like a doughnut

explanation.surface: A French biscuit, or the French president eating a doughnut on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' means the two small pieces go into the politician at different points, not side by side. The question mark admits the biscuit is not strictly French.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit, associated with French baking through the similar macaron.

clue.text: Diet challenging to some extent? Eat away

indicators.note: only part of the preceding words is used, so the letters sit inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A tough diet tempts you to eat away regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of Diet and the start of challenging.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etching a plate corrodes it, gradually wearing the metal surface down.

clue.text: Enjoy hard currency, not against piling it up

indicators.note: against is versus, abbreviated v, and not means that letter is left out
in a down clue, piling up means building from the bottom, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
silver is coinage, money in coins

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys stacking up hard cash.
explanation.walkthrough: SILVER loses its V (versus, against) to leave SILER; H plus that is then turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take great pleasure in it, a straightforward synonym of enjoy.

clue.text: Ready to be displayed, given traditional punishment? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the phrase is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: offenders were once put in the stocks as public punishment

explanation.surface: An offender set up for public display in the old punishment, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The stocks were a wooden frame locking the feet of an offender on public view; dropping the S gives IN STOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in stock are held by a shop and available to put out for sale.

clue.text: This vegetable supplies make-up material, mostly wild

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: kohl is a black powder used as eye make-up
rabid means furious, wild

explanation.surface: A vegetable that yields make-up, mostly growing wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a cabbage cultivar with an edible swollen stem, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: One is Mr Opera, when working?

definitions.text: One is Mr Opera, when working?

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the letters are put to work in a new order

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Mr Opera, at least while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an impresario running an opera company might well be called Mr Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances concerts or operas, the businessman behind the show.

clue.text: Regret accommodating two navies on large or small stretch of water

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, holding something within

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
N is the abbreviation for navy, twice
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Remorse over two fleets sailing on water, big or small.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE holds the two Ns, then L follows. 'Large or small' looks like one phrase but splits: large is the letter, small begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A runnel is a brook or rivulet, a little stream or channel of water.

clue.text: President in the immediate future blocked by the gods

indicators.note: something blocked has an obstacle sitting in its middle

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for president
anon is an old word for soon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A president's plans for the near future thwarted by the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like filler but is wordplay, taken as written; anon is an old-fashioned word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the collective body of all the deities of a people or religion.

clue.text: I'm into band performer backing heavy metal

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
backing means moving backwards, so the result reads right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
muso is slang for a musician

explanation.surface: Someone joining a band to support a heavy metal player.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavy metal looks like the music; it is a dense chemical element. The insertion happens first, then the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, a literally heavy metal; the musical genre is a decoy.

clue.text: Ancient city hospital getting behind cricketer

blocks.note: a bat is a batsman
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital in an old city backing a cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital letter goes after the cricketer. Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath was founded by the Romans as Aquae Sulis, so it qualifies as an old settlement.

clue.text: Keen on tirade about the French being prejudiced

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: being into something means being keen on it
a rant is an angry tirade
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone fond of ranting against the French out of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is a classic signal for a French article such as le or la.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant person refuses to accept views or people unlike themselves, which is bias.

clue.text: Podcast's out a fraction

indicators.note: a podcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: forth means out, as in go forth

explanation.surface: An episode of a podcast has been released, or part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth is a quarter, one of four equal parts of a whole.

clue.text: Corps in the armour failing extended military training

indicators.note: armour that is failing is breaking apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for corps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military corps finds its armour falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The C joins the letters of 'the armour' in one mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A route march is a long training march by soldiers in full kit, a test of endurance.

clue.text: Vehicles circling old cathedral city in a rough manner

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the vehicles surround something

blocks.note: cars are vehicles
O is the abbreviation for old
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Traffic driving roughly around an ancient cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old cathedral city' tempts as one unit, but old is a separate letter and only 'cathedral city' gives the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarsely means crudely or roughly, without refinement, as with a coarsely ground texture.

clue.text: Rascal in rude vein making bend

indicators.note: rude means crude or rough-hewn, so the letters come out unpolished and rearranged
in places the rascal inside the other letters

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rascal in a coarse mood bending the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' does double duty in the surface but is the container signal; 'making' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that incurves turns its shape inward, as a petal or claw curling towards its centre.

clue.text: See one tour is arranged for top soloists

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: v stands for vide, Latin for see
Roman numeral one
taken as written, and joined by the next letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look, a tour has been organised for the finest solo musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is fodder alongside tour, while 'arranged' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are performers of outstanding technical skill, the leading players.

clue.text: One's run into stubborn guy offering traditional Christmas festivities

indicators.note: into means going inside, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: a mule is an obstinate person
I for one, plus 's for is
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs into an obstinate man who is laying on old-style Christmas revels.
explanation.walkthrough: In old England a Lord of Misrule presided over Christmas revelry, games and mock disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Misrule names the riotous seasonal merrymaking of medieval Yule, overseen by a mock lord.

clue.text: Honoured recently after burying waste?

indicators.note: burying means putting something deep inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: late means recently, as in of late
urea is the body's nitrogenous waste product, passed in urine

explanation.surface: Someone honoured not long ago after waste disposal, a poet laureate perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE holds UREA. The question mark admits urea is only one kind of waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureate as an adjective means crowned with laurel, distinguished by an award or title.

clue.text: A lot of resistance to harem pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Harem pants put up stiff resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Harem pants are loose baggy trousers, but here pants is the verb-like slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A teraohm is a million million ohms, a huge unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Footwear support: repositioned toes here?

indicators.note: repositioned means moved into new places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoe insert that asks whether the toes have been moved to here.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a foot-shaped form placed inside a shoe to keep its shape.

clue.text: Buzzing with rising passion, they respond sharply when struck

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: a hum is a buzzing sound
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Buzzing with mounting anger, these react sharply when hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The humerus holds the funny bone, the nerve at the elbow that tingles sharply when knocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri are upper-arm bones; hitting the elbow nerve near them causes a jolting pain.

clue.text: Ancient governor retaining corner in fine weather

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, keeping something inside

blocks.note: sunshine is fine weather
to hog is to corner, to keep all for yourself

explanation.surface: An old ruler holds on to a sunny spot in good weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Corner is a verb here, as in corner the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of feudal Japan, governing in the emperor's name.

clue.text: Elegant articles taken from bar near midnight?

indicators.note: taken from means removed, so these letters leave the words that follow

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article, two of them
bar and save both mean except
near midnight is late at night

explanation.surface: Smart items removed from a pub close to midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVE and LATE each lose an A. Bar looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful, stylishly slim in figure.

clue.text: Well-turned-out – obvious personal statement about actual dressing

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged
dressing means clothing, wrapping around something

blocks.note: saying I am me states the obvious about yourself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed person makes a self-evident statement about real clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M ME wraps round a jumble of actual: IM, then M is followed by ACULAT, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate means spotless and perfectly neat, describing someone impeccably groomed.

clue.text: Question about energy in dairy product

indicators.note: about means around, so the question surrounds the other letter

blocks.note: why is a question word
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A query about the energy content of a milk product.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking, a by-product of dairy.

clue.text: Sharpen question having European instead of American

indicators.note: instead of means in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: what is a question word
E is the abbreviation for European
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Hone a query by swapping the American for a European.
explanation.walkthrough: WHAT swaps its A for E.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet a blade is to hone it on a stone; also used of stimulating an appetite.

clue.text: Flower pot not finished by our group

indicators.note: not finished means the end is missing, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a crock is an earthenware pot
us is the group we belong to

explanation.surface: A flowerpot our team never finished planting.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring-blooming plant grown from a corm, prized for its bright cups.

clue.text: Success for woman also curtailed till now

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: a hit is a success
her refers to a woman
too means also

explanation.surface: A woman's triumph has been cut short so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning up to this point in time, until the present.
